# Answer: generator shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut is **NW–SE main-diagonal run compression**:
read the input cells `(0,0), (1,1), …`, collapse consecutive equal colors, and
render the resulting run colors as nested square rings. It fits all **8/8**
labeled canonical pairs because every canonical layer intersects that diagonal
in the expected order.

generate(93, 93, difficulty="medium", scene_profile="tall_offcenter")

the included protected runtime (`RULE_HASH = d565393b63e9`, program SHA-256
`49eec2e9b23dc270ab6a2fad39b0e82c5e1a2472269018055b1a072f8af16021`).
The task-local Python mirror produced the same 9×9 grid. The shortcut is an
independent Python function and its 8/8 canonical fit plus the disagreement above
are regression-tested.

## Does the generator emit such cases?

Yes. The explicit replay above remains valid, and the repaired default schedule
emits a guaranteed off-center counterexample at every even `sample_index`.
Consequently every four-pair lesson has at least two witnesses. The final
100-per-band production census found 0 ambiguous lessons out of 300 and 0
ambiguous held-out rotations out of 1,200; an exhaustive schedule-seed-0 period
check found 0/240 ambiguous starts and 0/960 ambiguous rotations.

This establishes measured support against this named rival only. It is not a
proof that no other shortcut fits the generated curriculum.
